mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a Ford Galaxy EcoBoost engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ford Galaxy EcoBoost engine replacement costs range from £1,200 for used 1.5 units to £5,500 for fully rebuilt 2.0 EcoBoost engines with 12-month warranty. Typical reconditioned 1.5 EcoBoost prices sit between £2,200-£3,400 supply-only, while 2.0 EcoBoost units range from £3,000-£4,500. Prices vary by engine code, year, and whether supply & fit is included.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EcoBoost engine failure in a Ford Galaxy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of EcoBoost engine failure in the Ford Galaxy are cold-start rattle (1.5 EcoBoost), rough idle and loss of power (carbon buildup), and engine management lights with camshaft position codes (2.0 EcoBoost VVT). Ignoring these symptoms can lead to catastrophic engine damage requiring full replacement.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a high-mileage Ford Galaxy EcoBoost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Ford Galaxy EcoBoost engine costs £2,200-£5,500 rebuilt, often representing better value than selling a high-mileage Galaxy with engine faults. With strong residual values on well-maintained Mk3 examples (£6,000-£22,000), engine replacement is economically sensible for vehicles with sound chassis and interior.

mainEntity.name: What engine code is in my Ford Galaxy EcoBoost and how do I check?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Ford Galaxy EcoBoost engine code appears on the engine block stamping, vehicle registration document, or via DVLA lookup using your registration number. Early 1.5 EcoBoost (2015-2018) carries UNCJ/UNCK, later 1.5 (2018-2023) uses C15HDTX, and 2.0 EcoBoost (2015-2023) uses R9CD/R9CI.

mainEntity.name: Do Ford Galaxy EcoBoost engines use timing chains or belts?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Ford Galaxy 1.5 EcoBoost uses a timing chain, while the 2.0 EcoBoost also uses a timing chain - neither uses a wet belt. However, timing chain tensioner wear on the 1.5 EcoBoost is a documented concern at higher mileage. Using the correct oil specification and adhering to service intervals is essential for timing system longevity.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a reconditioned Ford Galaxy EcoBoost engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reconditioned Ford Galaxy EcoBoost engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty covering parts and labour at any UK garage. Specialist rebuilders may offer extended 24-month coverage on EcoBoost units with upgraded timing components.

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Galaxy 1.5-2.0 EcoBoost - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Ford Galaxy 1.5 and 2.0 EcoBoost petrol engines brought turbocharged efficiency and refined power to the Mk3 Galaxy MPV, offering family buyers a compelling alternative to diesel. The 1.5 EcoBoost delivered excellent fuel economy for urban use, while the 2.0 EcoBoost provided effortless motorway cruising with up to 240hp.

milestones.description: **2015** - Mk3 Galaxy launched with 1.5 EcoBoost (UNCJ/UNCK, 160hp) and 2.0 EcoBoost (R9CD/R9CI, 240hp)
**2018** - 1.5 EcoBoost updated to C15HDTX (165hp) with revised emissions hardware
**2019** - 2.0 EcoBoost continues with R9CD/R9CI codes through to end of production
**2023** - Mk3 Galaxy production ends; EcoBoost variants discontinued

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Ford Galaxy 1.5-2.0 EcoBoost is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h3: The Ford Galaxy 1.5 and 2.0 EcoBoost petrol engines offer refined turbocharged performance, but timing chain tensioner wear on the 1.5 and carbon buildup on both variants are common replacement drivers as Mk3 examples enter higher mileage. Every rebuilt Galaxy EcoBoost engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded timing components and verified cylinder head condition, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. problems.group: Ford Galaxy 1.5 EcoBoost Timing Chain Tensioner Wear
problems.h4: Ford Galaxy 1.5 EcoBoost Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why Cold-Start Rattle Appears
problems.rootCause: The hydraulic timing chain tensioner can lose oil pressure due to sludge buildup or wear, causing chain slack and a characteristic rattle on cold start. This is exacerbated by extended oil change intervals or using incorrect oil viscosity.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain tensioner with updated unit, oil and filter change with correct specification
repairOptions.longevity: Resolves cold-start rattle. Highly cost-effective if caught early

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, guides, tensioner and VVT sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain has stretched or if tensioner failure has caused additional wear

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with bench-tested rebuilt unit, new timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only required if chain has jumped causing valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2015-2023 Ford Galaxy EcoBoost currently values between £6,000 and £22,000 in the UK used market. With rebuilt engine costs at £3,800-£5,200, replacement is viable for well-maintained examples with sound chassis and interior. For sub-£6,000 examples, a used engine or preventative tensioner service may offer better value.
problems.recommendation: At the first sign of cold-start rattle on your Galaxy 1.5 EcoBoost, have the timing chain tensioner inspected and replaced preventatively. Using the correct oil specification and adhering to Ford's service intervals is the single most important factor in preventing timing chain issues.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 1.5 EcoBoost engine prices for your Ford Galaxy

problems.h4: Ford Galaxy 1.5/2.0 EcoBoost Carbon Buildup - Why Direct Injection Engines Lose Power
problems.rootCause: Direct injection petrol engines do not wash the intake valves with fuel, allowing carbon deposits to accumulate on valve stems and intake ports. This restricts airflow, causes rough idle, misfires, and progressive power loss.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Intake manifold removal, walnut shell blasting of intake ports and valves, throttle body cleaning
repairOptions.longevity: Restores lost power and smoothness. Recommended every 50k-60k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Carbon cleaning plus injector servicing, PCV valve replacement, and fuel system treatment
repairOptions.longevity: Comprehensive solution for high-mileage vehicles showing multiple symptoms

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with bench-tested rebuilt unit, cleaned intake system, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only required if carbon buildup has caused valve damage or if engine has additional mechanical failure

problems.recommendation: Carbon cleaning is a cost-effective maintenance procedure that should be considered every 50,000-60,000 miles on Galaxy EcoBoost engines. If you notice rough idle, hesitation, or reduced fuel economy, have the intake system inspected. Replacement is only necessary if carbon buildup has caused valve damage.
problems.cta: -> Get Ford Galaxy EcoBoost carbon cleaning quotes

problems.group: Ford Galaxy 2.0 EcoBoost VVT Solenoid Failure
problems.h4: Ford Galaxy 2.0 EcoBoost VVT Solenoid Failure - Why Engine Management Lights Appear
problems.rootCause: The variable valve timing (VVT) solenoids can become clogged with oil sludge or fail electrically, causing camshaft position errors, reduced power, and engine management lights. This is often a symptom of infrequent oil changes.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of faulty VVT solenoid(s), oil and filter change, ECU adaptation reset
repairOptions.longevity: Resolves camshaft position errors. Highly cost-effective

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of both VVT solenoids, timing chain inspection, oil system flush
Complete engine swap with bench-tested rebuilt unit, new VVT components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only required if VVT failure has caused internal damage

problems.recommendation: If your Galaxy 2.0 EcoBoost displays an engine management light with camshaft position codes, have the VVT solenoids inspected and replaced. Regular oil changes with the correct specification are the best prevention.
